newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Fracmaster sees doubling earnings.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Fracmaster sees doubling earnings.

text.p: Oil services firm Canadian Fracmaster Ltd expects to double earnings in 1997, buoyed by booming North American drilling activity and an improved operating climate in Russia, President Les Margetak said on Wednesday.
Fracmaster was targeting 1997 earnings of C$1 a share, up from C$0.51 a share in 1996, Margetak told reporters after the annual meeting.
The company's fortunes had improved to the point where it was no longer considering the restructuring it was examining last year, he said.
"We chose not to split the company," Margetak said.
Amid uncertainty over the Russian oil scene in late 1995, Fracmaster's stock dropped to a low of 4.70 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
But the shares have recovered since October 1996 and closed on Wednesday up 0.75 to 15.35, a new year high.

"We had originally said that our Russian earnings picture would be similar in 1997 as it was in 1996 and that would be in and about C$20 million. We now think that will be closer to C$25 million," he said.
He said big improvements were expected as a result of Russia's abolishment of its oil export tariff and the narrowing of the domestic and export oil price gap.
The company was also expected to reap rewards from a growing fee-for-service business in Russia, he said.
Fracmaster was targeting 700 fee-for-service well stimulation jobs in the country this year. That would be up from 254 jobs in 1996 and 12 jobs in 1995.
Margetak declined to reveal the value that ING-Barings placed on Fracmaster's Russian operations.

In North America, Margetak said this year's strong oil and gas drilling activity was expected to "mark the beginning of a multi-year growth trend" for its drilling chemicals and coiled tubing businesses.
The company's acquisition of Matrix Well Services in April for an undisclosed sum made it Canada's largest provider of coiled tubing services, a quickly expanding market.

In the U.S., American Fracmaster -- which the company set up last year with a group of private investors -- had a target of capturing five percent of the oil pumping services market in Texas, Louisiana and New Mexico, which would result in C$50 million in gross revenues, Margetak said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))

In 1996, Fracmaster retained ING-Barings as financial adviser to find ways to boost the value of its operations in Russia, where it takes oil in return for well stimulation services in various joint ventures and provides a growing number of fee-for-service oil well stimulation operations.
One option the company explored was spinning off Russian operations into a separate publicly traded company.

"The attitude toward Russian investment, I think it's safe to say, has changed in the North American market. We were trading over C$15 today, which is back to our IPO price and we're realizing value that way," Margetak said.
